shifts.summary: The paper was reported as moderate overall. Reasoning was described as easy by some and moderate by others, giving an easy to moderate range. intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 24 October 2026 was reported as having a moderate overall difficulty level. Reasoning was described as ranging from easy to moderate, while Quantitative Aptitude was largely viewed as difficult. English was consistently reported as easy and General Awareness had no clear difficulty rating. All figures mentioned are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1, which has been reported, indicated a moderate overall difficulty level. Shifts 2 and 3 are still pending and no overall assessment is available for them yet.

faqs.q: How was the Quantitative Aptitude section perceived on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: In the reported Shift 1, Quantitative Aptitude was mostly described as difficult, with one report labeling it as hard. No data is available for Shifts 2 and 3 at this time.

faqs.q: What does the analysis say about the English section on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: The English section was consistently reported as easy in Shift 1. No usable analysis has been published for Shifts 2 and 3 yet.

faqs.q: Is there any analysis available for Shift 2 of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 24 October 2026?
faqs.a: No usable analysis has been published for Shift 2 yet. A review will be added when sufficient candidate evidence becomes available.

faqs.a: The figures presented are unofficial; SSC normalises scores across shifts, and the reported numbers should be treated as indicative rather than official.
